learningObjectives: Manipulate strings using indexing, slicing, and built-in methods.
Format dynamic text using modern Python string formatting.
Apply string processing techniques to practical text-based problems.

activities.title: String Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore indexing and slicing in a Python string.

content.concept: Strings are ordered sequences of characters. Indexing accesses one character, while slicing extracts a portion of the string.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Extracts characters from index 1 up to, but not including, index 4: yth.

activities.title: Slice Explorer
activities.instruction: Adjust the slice boundaries to extract the required text.

content.concept: The syntax text[start:stop:step] controls which characters are selected. The stop index is excluded.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: String Method Explorer
activities.instruction: Choose the method that best solves each text-processing task.

content.concept: Methods such as strip(), lower(), replace(), and split() provide reusable operations for processing text.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: strip() → remove leading and trailing whitespace
lower() → split text into a list
split() → replace one substring with another
config.answer: strip() → remove leading and trailing whitespace

activities.title: F-String Builder
activities.instruction: Build a formatted message using an f-string.

content.concept: F-strings allow expressions and variable values to be embedded directly inside string literals using braces.
